conviction_note: Q3 numbers are new (no profit warning, no trading update) but there is no sourced consensus, so the findings are capped small. The only real lean is a possible buyback, which the board said in August it was evaluating and Pareto flags as a catalyst. Against it sit a peer's (Lea Bank) higher Q3 credit losses in Norway and this name's mixed print reactions (+2.2, -5.7, +3.5, -2.6). So p_up is 53 on an abs move of 5.0, giving +0.3, while the findings sum to +0.7. The gap exists because the buyback finding is a conditional event, not a measured number.

new_in_release.expect: Q3 numbers are new. Seasonally Q3 is NOBA's lowest-credit-loss quarter (CEO comment on Q3 2025), plus a modest NPL-sale gain. A small beat is likely but unsourced.
The first Q4 interim dividend under the policy (40% of 9M adjusted core profit, approved by an EGM); roughly SEK 2.5/share by my arithmetic. Mechanical and expected.
A buyback decision is possible. A positive surprise if announced; mild disappointment if the board is still 'evaluating'.
NOBA guides only medium-term targets. I expect them reiterated, with cost growth declining from Q4. A change in either direction would be the larger mover.

findings.finding: The board said in the Q2 report it is evaluating a share buyback 'to manage surplus capital generation', with no decision yet. The Q3 report is the first scheduled venue. Peer Norion announced a SEK 500m buyback with its Q3 on 2026-10-22 and rose 3.5% that day, and Pareto names a buyback as a positive driver.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior NOBA buyback. When the extra dividend of SEK 1.50 was announced with the FY2025 report on 2026-02-04, the stock fell 5.7% (on other lines too). Peer Norion's buyback-plus-Q3 day was +3.5%.
findings.original_quote: NOBA's Board of Directors is evaluating the possibility of a share buyback programme. No decision has yet been made, and the market will be continuously informed about the progress of this process.
findings.why_not_priced: Not fully priced, because it is a decision nobody outside the board knows yet. It may be partly priced: the stock is up 6.5% over 20 days and 4.0% over 5 days into the print, and Pareto's 27 Oct preview put it on the wire. CET1 was 13.4% at Q2, inside the 13-15% target, so a large programme is not a given. A market that had priced a certain buyback would already sit near the 113-121 SEK targets; at 92.1 it does not.
findings.independence: Pareto preview (Finwire, 2026-10-27): 'Pareto ser även ett möjligt aktieåterköpsprogram som en positiv kursdrivare' https://www.placera.se/telegram/noba-bank-pareto-hojer-riktkursen-for-noba-till-115-kronor-upprepar-kop-20261027 ; Norion's peer buyback: https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b49670b4e611e01a2ba1757830dac4284&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Peer Lea Bank's Q3 (22 Oct) showed its credit loss level rising to 3.9% (3.7%). It called Q3 'normally a seasonally weaker quarter for collection, which reduces recoveries on non-performing loans', with Norway its largest book. That points against a continued fall in NOBA's (Bank Norwegian's) loss level. NOBA fell 3.9% the same day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit losses have been NOBA's beat line: nine consecutive quarters of lower loss levels per the Q2 report. The Q2 release day was -2.6% then +3.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a proxy, probably partly priced: NOBA fell 3.9% on 2026-10-22, the same day as Lea's report (-4.3%) and Avarda (-2.8%). It also conflicts with NOBA's own history of Q3 being its most favourable credit-loss quarter, and Norion's Q3 loss level fell (1.6% vs 1.7%). It is sized small for those reasons.
findings.independence: Contradicted rather than corroborated: Norion Q3 credit loss level 1.6% (1.7) https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b49670b4e611e01a2ba1757830dac4284&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: NPL portfolio sales of ~SEK 400m gross in Norway, Denmark and Finland were signed in Q2 with an 'expected positive impact on earnings in the third quarter'. This is a disclosed one-off inside Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to an NPL-sale gain at NOBA. European beats built on one-offs have been sold (H&M, per the lessons file).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The company disclosed it in August, so every estimate carrying a Q3 number has it. It is worth something only if the gain is larger than modelled, and the size of the gain was never given.

findings.finding: Per its dividend policy footnote, NOBA's Q4 dividend is based on adjusted core profit for the first nine months and approved by an EGM. So the Q3 report should carry the first such proposal, about 40% of 9M core profit (roughly SEK 2.5/share).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The May dividend (1.60 ordinary + 1.50 extra) was announced with the FY report, a -5.7% day.
findings.original_quote: The dividend distributed during the fourth quarter is based on the adjusted core profit attributable to shareholders generated during the first nine months of the fiscal year and is resolved upon by an extraordinary general meeting.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It follows mechanically from a published policy and lands inside what the company guided. It is filed only because it is a sourced fact on this print, and an extra dividend on top would be the only surprise.

findings.finding: Pareto lifted 2026-28 EPS by 1-2% on currency-driven loan growth: Q3 FX translation of the NOK/EUR books lifts reported SEK lending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth has printed at 11-12% for several quarters with no outsized reaction.
findings.original_quote: Pareto höjer sina prognoser för vinst per aktie med 1-2 procent för 2026-2028, främst till följd av valutadriven utlåningstillväxt.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: it is on the wire and already in at least one estimate. It stays near 0 because FX translation does not change the local-currency growth that the market reads.

lessons_applied: 'Size the move on what is new; let reaction history move p_up, not abs': the Q3 numbers are new (no pre-release), so abs_move_pct went from 4.5 to 5.0. It stays below the 7% European base because this is a well-covered bank with print reactions of 2-6%.
'A beat made of a one-off is sold': the NPL-sale gain finding went from +0.2 to +0.1.
'A zero on a read register is the truncation floor': positioning_check states there is no anchor and that the lean is the run-up.
